claim: SS La Suisse is a 1910 Belle Époque paddle steamer, 78.5m long, 850-passenger capacity, fully restored in 2009 and based on the Upper Lake route from Lausanne.
quote: La Suisse... commissioned in 1910... the most beautiful steam boat in the world... capacity 850 passengers, length 78.5 meters... underwent a complete renovation in 2009.

claim: From Lausanne, SS La Suisse sails three times daily to St-Gingolph returning via the Lavaux vineyards, a roughly three-hour circular cruise, with stops at Vevey, Montreux and Château de Chillon.
quote: La Suisse cruises three times per day from Lausanne to St Gingolph and on to Chateau de Chillon before returning to Lausanne via the Lavaux, with three hours for the full circular cruise.

claim: CGN paddle-steamer cruises cost the same as the modern boats; a 2-hour Geneva afternoon cruise is CHF 33 (CHF 46 first class) and a Geneva–Lausanne return day ticket is CHF 64 (CHF 90 first class); Swiss rail passes and Half Fare Card are accepted.
quote: A 2-hour lunchtime or afternoon cruise on a paddle steamer from Geneva costs CHF33 (CHF46 First Class)... a day ticket costs CHF64 (CHF90 in first class)... Most Swiss railway and transportation discount passes and travel cards are accepted on CGN Lac Léman boats.

claim: Ouchy's tree-lined quays — first opened in 1901 — run from the Haldimand tower past Château d'Ouchy and continue east toward Lutry and west to Saint-Sulpice, with three gardens (Denantou, Elysée, Olympic Park) and a rose garden of 130+ species at Place du Général Guisan.
quote: richly flowered and tree-lined quays, first opened in 1901... promenade extends eastward toward Lutry and westward to Saint-Sulpice... Rose garden at Place du Général Guisan featuring more than 130 different species of rose.

claim: Ouchy is reached by the city's vertical M2 metro and offers pedalo rentals, biking, water-skiing lessons and views across to the Savoy Alps.
quote: Ouchy is a lakefront district in Lausanne, Switzerland, accessible via the city's vertical m2 metro from the train station... Pedalo rentals, Biking, Water skiing lessons... The Savoy-Alps summits are visible across the lake.

claim: Bellerive-Plage opens May 18 to Sept 1 (09:30–20:00) and Sept 2–16 (09:30–19:30), with an Olympic pool, a 10m diving board, three pools and a 350m supervised lake beach, plus volleyball, basketball and food kiosks.
quote: May 18 – September 1: 9:30 AM – 8:00 PM daily; September 2 – 16: 9:30 AM – 7:30 PM daily... three large pools, one with a ten-metre diving board... supervised lake beach spanning 350 meters.

claim: Plage de Vidy is the largest beach on Lake Geneva with over 500m of sand across multiple coves, set in Parc Louis Bourget with showers, playgrounds, volleyball, and rentals for stand-up paddleboards and pedal boats; entry is free.
quote: Vidy Beach is the largest beach and green space on Lake Geneva with over 500 metres of sand across multiple small coves... Water sports rentals (standup paddleboards, pedal boats)... Parc Louis Bourget, 1006 Lausanne.

claim: Bateaux-Location-Ouchy rents 4- and 5-seater pedal boats (with optional slide) next to the Ouchy port at CHF 15/30 min, CHF 25/hour, CHF 45/2 hours; life jackets and parasols are free, unaccompanied children must be 14+.
quote: 30 minutes: CHF 15; 60 minutes: CHF 25; 90 minutes: CHF 38; 2 hours: CHF 45... Life jackets and parasols provided free of charge... Unaccompanied children must be at least 14 years old.

claim: The M2 between Ouchy and Flon is a fully automated rubber-tyred line that opened in 2008 with a maximum 11.6% gradient — among the world's steepest metro lines — using MP89CA trains akin to Paris Métro Line 14.
quote: maximum gradient of 11.6% (1 in 8.66) on the Ouchy-Flon section... opened in 2008... fully automated... 15 two-car MP89CA trains, similar to those on Line 14 of the Paris Métro.

claim: The Lausanne M2 line is 5.9 km long across 14 stations, full run about 20 minutes, linking Ouchy on the lake to Lausanne railway station and the Flon hub where M1 and the LEB regional rail interchange.
quote: The Lausanne Métro Line M2 is 5.9 kilometres (3.7 mi) long... links the lakeside at Ouchy with Lausanne railway station and the core of the city at Flon. At Lausanne-Flon, passengers can transfer to M1 and the R20 service of leb... 14 stations, and the full running time is about 20 minutes.
